description: Change semantics for the module-level fields that no provider service owns.
_note: ADR-020 D9 / issue #567. module-fields.json declares 74 fields; 55 name a '<module>:<service>' coordinate in their usedBy and are classified by that service's services/<svc>/fields.json. The 19 here name none — their usedBy is empty or 'general' — so they describe the MODULE itself (its provenance, lifecycle and wiring) rather than anything a provider configures, and until now nothing declared what changing them costs. This manifest is DECLARATION ONLY: no code consumes it yet. module-manager's pre-gate still waves every one of these through as 'config-only' without consulting a class, which is why setting kind, location or installTime by hand is currently accepted. Teaching the pre-gate to refuse on this manifest — the way network-manager already refuses a zone field with no changeClass in zones-fields.json — is issue #567, deliberately deferred until ADR-020 has landed across the estate. No entry carries a liveKey: there is no report-service.sh for module-level fields, because there is no provider to ask. Every entry is therefore apply:'none' — for these fields, writing the config IS the change. That makes 'in-place' here mean 'takes effect at once, nothing to refuse' rather than 'the converge applies it live'; converge.ts already calls this situation 'config-only', and #567 may be the moment that becomes a real class.

description.changeNote: Pushed to the Proxmox summary page when the guest is created and never pushed again, so an edit after install changes config only. Classed by what changing it COSTS (nothing, no disruption), not by today's gap — `qm set --description` works on a live VM, so a hook would make this a real `set` under cluster:vm.

displayName.changeNote: Read by the identity services when they ensure the module's tile on the start page; a change shows at the module's next update. Nothing on the guest changes.

version.changeNote: Written by the release: the module's own semver, carried in at install and update and read to decide whether an upgrade exists. Not changed by hand.

appVersion.changeNote: Written by the release: the upstream version the module deploys, carried in at install and update. Not changed by hand.

releaseDate.changeNote: Written by the release: when this version of the module was released. Not changed by hand.

maintainer.changeNote: Written by the release: who maintains the module. Not changed by hand.

status.changeNote: Written by the release: a maturity the module's author claims in its own JSON, carried in at install and update. Not changed by hand; archiving a deployment is `management`.

suspended.changeNote: Written by 'module-manager suspend' and 'resume', which stop and start the guest with it; set by hand it would say a running guest is paused, or hide a stopped one from the update and the health check.

tier.changeNote: RETIRED (ADR-022e): scope follows `stack`. Written by the release when a config still carries it; not changed by hand.

source.changeNote: Written by the install: the trust marker inferred from the catalogue repository. Not changed by hand.

rebootOk.changeNote: The ADR-020 D8 disruption authorization. Nothing APPLIES it — the converge READS it to decide whether an unattended pass may reboot or offline-migrate this guest. Default false, so silence never authorizes downtime.

sshPort.changeNote: Applied by the satellite's own update.sh, which the converge after `modify --set` runs: the OPNsense port forward and edge rule, the satellite's firewall and nginx re-provisioned — sessions on :443/:80 and the admin VPN see a restart of a few seconds. Off (0) removes all of it. Set it together with sshAllow; check-config.sh refuses it alone.

sshAllow.changeNote: Applied by the satellite's own update.sh: its firewall and nginx re-provisioned with the new list (a restart of a few seconds for the relays). Inert while sshPort is off.

sshKeyOnly.changeNote: Applied by the machine module's own update.sh, which the converge after `modify --set` runs: ssh-key-only.sh writes or removes one sshd drop-in and reloads sshd, which drops no open session — no disruption, nothing to authorize (#756). No hook: the module's update is the apply, as for every module-level field.

config.changeNote: The Pattern-A container, not a value: normalized to the flat form at deploy and at validation, so it has no state of its own. Listed for coverage — every schema field is classified or the manifest is incomplete.

dependsOn.changeNote: install-service.sh and delete-service.sh run off the DELTA `module-manager module modify` computes across the 3-way merge (the union of dependsOn+integratesWith before vs after). A `--set` writes the DEPLOYED side, so before and after agree, the delta is empty, and no service script runs — the config then claims a dependency that was never wired, or drops one whose wiring is still in place. Change it in the SOURCE module file and run `module-manager module modify`.

integratesWith.changeNote: As dependsOn, but optional: a provider that is not installed is ignored rather than blocking, and its install auto-wires pre-existing integrators. Same delta mechanism, so the same caveat applies.

provides.changeNote: What OTHER modules may declare a dependency on. Removing an entry breaks every consumer's resolution, which is why this is not a free edit even though nothing local changes.

environment.changeNote: Written by copy-update-json.sh --environment (ADR-007 P5). `module-manager module modify` and `module-manager module delete` resolve the SOURCE module file through it, so a wrong value points the lifecycle at the wrong module.

icon.changeNote: Read by the identity services, which upload the file under a content-hashed name and point the module's tile at it; a change shows at the module's next update.

moduleSource.changeNote: Written by copy-update-json.sh (was `location`, #609). get_module_dir() reads it as the SOLE source of the module directory and returns success for any path that exists — so a wrong value does not fail loudly, it silently runs the lifecycle against the wrong directory.

location.changeNote: Where a machine is: a location of the site (site-manager location list), checked at the write. Changing it moves nothing; it changes where the topology and the console draw the machine and what backup-manager validate's off-site check compares with the site. A value with a '/' is the pre-#609 name of moduleSource and is never written.

kind.changeNote: Changing what type of workload a module is — a vm into an lxc — is a rebuild, not an edit, so `modify --set kind=…` is refused; change it in the module's source JSON. No provider reads it back from the live system, so the converge never compares it.

installTime.changeNote: Stamped by copy-update-json.sh at install. Reporting only; never re-derived.

updateTime.changeNote: Bumped by `module-manager module modify` on every successful update. Reporting only.

variant.changeNote: RETIRED, superseded by `environment`. Never write it; installs strip it (copy-update-json.sh del(.variant)). Retained in module-fields.json only so a pre-migration config carrying it is classified rather than reported unknown.

physicalLocation.changeNote: RETIRED: a machine names its location (`location`). Migration 0021 moves it; never write it.

uplinks.changeNote: A node's lan/wan ports (#40). Writing it changes nothing on the node; converging it re-carries the lan bridge, which drains the node first — `site-manager node network set <node> --apply` does both, one node at a time, under a rollback. Until then health-manager reports the drift.

stack.changeNote: Written by the release: the stack the catalogue lists the module under. Not changed by hand; moving a module is a release change.

roles.changeNote: What a machine is for (ADR-022h). Nothing re-provisions the machine when it changes: a satellite's roles are rendered onto it at install, so a new set takes `module-manager module delete <instance> --decommission` and an add. The `backup` role is set by `module modify <instance> --lockdown`, never by --set (ADR-010 §8.4).

address.changeNote: Where the mothership reaches a machine; changing it re-points TAPPaaS, it does not move the machine.

management.changeNote: Takes a module in or out of TAPPaaS's lifecycle; nothing is applied to the module itself.

assistantModel.changeNote: Read by the console's backend when it chooses the assistant's LiteLLM model; a change is picked up at its next status check (within five minutes). Nothing on any guest changes.

publicDomain.changeNote: A DNS name for a raw-port service (TURN, SMTP, …). Nothing on the cluster reflects it directly: the module that reads it (coturn) re-derives what its consumers see on their next converge, and the operator re-points the public A record. No guest is touched.

woodpeckerAdmins.changeNote: Read by woodpecker.nix from the module's companion JSON: the module's update rebuilds its NixOS configuration and restarts the server with the new list. Nothing else changes.

controllers.changeNote: What the control plane links and registers for this module: a change adds or removes a controller other modules' managers drive, so it is made in the module's JSON and released, never set on a running site.

managers.changeNote: What the control plane links and registers for this module: a change adds or removes verbs operators and the console use, so it is made in the module's JSON and released.
